newsitem.title: UK: MED, W.AFRICA SUEZMAXES, MIDEAST/JAPAN VLCCS FIRM.
newsitem.headline: MED, W.AFRICA SUEZMAXES, MIDEAST/JAPAN VLCCS FIRM.

text.p: Chartering rates for 250,000 tonne Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs) from the Mideast to Japan were firm again on Tuesday amid good enquiry for liftings of Iraqi crude out of Mina al Bakr, shipbrokers said.
Dealers said Jomo's fixture of the 250,000 tonne Kashimasan Maru at a blistering W89.75 was a sign of continued strength in the market.
Dealers also saw a number of fixtures on subjects out of Mina al Bakr on older vessels for westwards voyages although brokers differed as to the number of ships that had been chartered.

Demand for Suezmaxes to take Iraqi crude out of Ceyhan into the Med kept the pressure on charterers to pay high prices to owners to carry their oil. A number of fresh fixtures were seen at around W90-95, unchanged from Monday's levels.
Suezmaxes seeking to take West African cargoes to the U.S. Gulf saw rates a good five points firmer from last week.
Sun's fixture of the 130,000 tonne Czantoria at W87.50 for early September loading, and of the 135,000 tonne Tito Tapias at W84 were indicative of new levels of chartering.
Aframax markets in the UK/Cont region were buoyant.
A number of 80,000 tonne vessels were fixed for late August for destinations within the region at around W100.
